summary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment redefining 14th Amendment citizenship so that only children born in the US to at least one citizen, US national, or lawful permanent resident parent would be citizens.

scores.thoughts: The bill proposes a constitutional amendment redefining birthright citizenship under the 14th Amendment. It contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures of any kind.
The bill is exclusively about citizenship qualifications and contains no tax-related language, rates, credits, or revenue measures.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, public programs, or market structures.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The core purpose of the bill is to amend the Constitution to limit birthright citizenship to children with at least one parent who is a U.S. citizen, national, or lawful permanent resident. This directly narrows automatic citizenship for children of non-citizens and undocumented immigrants, constituting a significant restriction on immigration-related legal status and pathways.
No references to reproductive rights, abortion access, or related constitutional interpretations.
The bill does not address military funding, defense policy, or armed forces matters.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate provisions are present.
While citizenship status can indirectly affect eligibility for benefits, the bill itself makes no changes to welfare programs, eligibility rules, or safety-net funding.
Citizenship can influence educational access in practice, but the bill contains no education policy, funding, or school-choice provisions.
No content related to controlled substances, enforcement, or decriminalization.
The measure addresses constitutional citizenship language only and does not touch sentencing, policing, or criminal procedure.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions exist.
The bill has no fiscal, deficit, or debt-reduction components.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ legal protections or rights.
The legislation does not address foreign assistance or international aid.
Citizenship determines voting eligibility, but the bill does not alter voting procedures, access, or election integrity rules.
No technology, data, or privacy regulations are involved.
The bill contains nothing related to employment, worker protections, or union matters.
No religious exemptions, civil-rights balancing, or anti-discrimination language appears.
